official_terms.name: extracellular region

definition.text: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

official_terms.comment: Note that this term is intended to annotate gene products that are not attached to the cell surface. For gene products at the cell surface, consider annotating to external side of plasma membrane ; GO:0009897.

definition.text: A collagen heterotrimer containing type VI alpha chains in alpha1(VI)alpha2(VI)alpha3(VI) trimers; type VI collagen triple helices associate to form beaded fibrils.

official_terms.name: extracellular matrix structural constituent

definition.text: The action of a molecule that contributes to the structural integrity of the extracellular matrix.

official_terms.comment: Extracellular matrix glycoproteins may be annotated to this term. PMID:24443019

definition.text: Binding to an integrin.
A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an extracellular matrix.
Any process that determines the size and arrangement of collagen fibrils within an extracellular matrix.
The volume enclosed by the membranes of the endoplasmic reticulum.
Binding to an identical protein or proteins.

Binding to collagen, a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals. Collagen is highly enriched in glycine (some regions are 33% glycine) and proline, occurring predominantly as 3-hydroxyproline (about 20%).

definition.text: Binds to and stops, prevents or reduces the activity of a serine-type endopeptidase.
Any vesicle that is part of the extracellular region.

A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

Extracellular matrix components occurring independently or along with elastin. Thought to have force-bearing functions in tendon. In addition to fibrillins, microfibrils may contain microfibrillar-Associated Proteins (MFAPs): MFAP1, MFAP2 (also known as MAGP-1), MFAP3, MFAP4, and MFAP5 (also known as MAGP-2).
A structure lying external to one or more cells, which provides structural support, biochemical or biomechanical cues for cells or tissues.
Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a glucose stimulus.

The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The muscle is an organ consisting of a tissue made up of various elongated cells that are specialized to contract and thus to produce movement and mechanical work.
A family of collagens containing multiple von Willebrand factor A (vWA) domains.
Binding to hyaluronic acid, a polymer composed of repeating dimeric units of glucuronic acid and N-acetyl glucosamine.

Binding to heparin, a member of a group of glycosaminoglycans found mainly as an intracellular component of mast cells and which consist predominantly of alternating alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galactose and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-6-sulfate residues.
A collagen heterotrimer containing type VI alpha chains in alpha1(VI)alpha2(VI)alpha3(VI) trimers; type VI collagen triple helices associate to form beaded fibrils.
